config.title: Default Configuration
config.intro: This app runs on one PC. Map the three folders every run needs, wherever they are on this PC. A runtime here uses them where they are; a pod carries them on its volume and links the paths the project's own files name onto them, so graphs and scripts run unchanged. The full story: docs/MOUNT-POINTS.md.
config.runpodHint: the account the app creates pods in
config.apiKeyStored: Stored ({hint}); enter a new one to replace it. Kept in {source}.
config.apiKeyUnset: Not set. From runpod.io, Settings, API Keys; stored on this PC only, never shown again.
config.volumeHint: the network volume that carries the three folders when a pod runs them
config.volumeIdHelp: Empty: the pod gets only its own disk and nothing above resolves.
config.mountPathHelp: Where the volume appears in the pod.
config.datacenterHelp: Must match the volume's datacenter. S3 marks the ones whose volumes take uploads with no pod running; the cards and prices are what a volume pod pays there (secure cloud).
config.imageHelp: What every new pod boots: ours, with the packs and the entrypoint that makes the links. It must be pushed to a registry first; a bare local name is refused at pod creation.
config.idleHelp: Stop a pod after this long with nothing queued. 0 = never.
config.foldersHint: the three every run uses, then any of your own; the exact links a pod makes are in the pod preview below. Mode {mode} (COMFY_MODE); {rule}
config.ruleProd: every folder is required in prod
config.ruleConfig: the switches say which are required in dev
config.requiredProd: prod mode: every folder is required
config.missing: This folder does not exist on this PC.
config.mirror: This is Binc's mirror, read-only by rule, and a run writes here. Map a folder of your own{hint}.
config.mirrorTree: or a copy of the tree
config.noRoot: The tree's job files and structure page name no root; a pod cannot link what its graphs name.
config.noDeclared: The tree names no path for it; nothing is linked on a pod.
config.customLinkHelp: optional: a pod links it onto the pod path
config.applyDefault: Apply to new pods by default
config.applyDefaultHint: (the pod form can switch it off per pod)
config.dryRunHint: (pods are simulated: nothing reaches RunPod, nothing bills; for testing the app)
config.previewLocal: What a runtime on this PC receives (as saved)
config.previewPod: What a new pod receives (as saved)
config.noVolume: no network volume: per-pod disk only
config.registryAuthHelp: For a private registry: the id of the credential saved on RunPod (Settings, Container registry auth). Leave empty for a public image.
config.podIntro: This pod’s own configuration, started from the Default Configuration. Everything here applies to this pod only: the volume, datacenter, image, idle stop, folders and links. The Default Configuration is not changed.
config.podOwn: This pod has its own configuration
config.volumeMissing: RunPod has no network volume with this id.

volumes.title: Network volumes
volumes.intro: A network volume is a disk in one RunPod datacenter that pods mount at /workspace. It bills whether or not a pod runs; a pod stopped on it bills nothing. Every pod the app creates attaches the Default Configuration's volume unless its own configuration names another.
volumes.none: No network volumes on this account.
volumes.s3Title: Takes uploads over RunPod's S3 API with no pod running (ADR-007).
volumes.viaConfig: Named by this pod's own configuration; a recreate attaches it
volumes.deleteBlocked: A pod is attached: delete or recreate that pod first.
volumes.confirmDelete: Delete the volume "{name}" ({size} GB) and everything on it? This cannot be undone.
volumes.name: Volume name
volumes.createHelp: About ${cost} a month at 0.07 per GB. A volume only grows afterwards, never shrinks, and never leaves its datacenter. S3-marked datacenters take uploads with no pod running.
